title: Mini OKR Vignette & Weekly Check — Kai Mendoza
content:
Notes to self: quick vignette-style log for a 3-week micro-OKR experiment. Keep it scrappy — this is for me to iterate on daily and share with Aria for coaching.

Why this experiment
- I'm getting pulled into too many partial tasks (context-switch tax). Goal: increase time in deep work and measurable impact per week.
- Hypothesis: if I commit to tighter, measurable KRs (3-week horizon) and block 3x 90-min deep slots, my deliverable throughput (PRs merged with tests) and unblock ratio will improve.

Mini-OKR (3-week window)
Objective: Move from scattered sprint noise to two high-impact deliverables that reduce latency-debug time and prevent regressions.
KR1: Merge 2 feature PRs that add end-to-end tests + bench harness for serving runtime (target: 2 merged w/ green CI).
KR2: Reduce my average task context switches per day from ~6 to <=3 (measure via calendar + toggl tags).
KR3: Decrease mean time to diagnose perf regressions for my area from 5h -> 2h (tracked in INF-2214 notes).

Baseline & tracking approach
- Baseline week (last 4 weeks): PRs merged with tests: 0.8/week. Context switches/day (manual sample): ~6.
- Measurement: manual log each day in this doc + short Toggl tag 'deep:kai', calendar focus blocks counted. Use brief daily status line: "D: PR/in-progress; C: #context-switches; T: blocks done".

Week 1 (2025-02-11 -> 2025-02-17) — quick check-in
- Progress: spun up bench harness prototype; initial PR branch created (WIP). 1x 90-min deep block completed on Tue, 2x on Thu.
- Metrics: PRs: 0 merged; Context switches/day sampled: Mon 5, Tue 4, Wed 6, Thu 3, Fri 7 -> avg ~5.0 (some improvement).
- Qualitative: felt good during Tue block, Thu block degenerated by Slack threads. Need better distraction containment.
- Blockers: waiting on infra token rotation to run bench end-to-end (INF-2214). Talked to SRE but not yet resolved.

Week 2 (2025-02-18 -> 2025-02-24) — quick check-in
- Progress: Bench harness integrated with local runner; added 2 smoke tests. Open PR created and assigned to Devon for review.
- Metrics: PRs merged: 0; contextual switches/day sample: Mon 3, Tue 2, Wed 4, Thu 3, Fri 2 -> avg 2.8 (goal for KR2 hit this week). Deep slots: 4/5 completed.
- Qualitative: blocking infra issue escalated -> SRE implemented temporary credential; I could run end-to-end. Felt momentum.
- Risks: PRs still need a follow-up to add trace sampling; may push one KR outside 3-week window.

Week 3 (2025-02-25 -> 2025-03-03) — quick check-in (current)
- Progress: One PR merged (feature + tests), green CI after rebase. Second PR in final review with Aria comments pending.
- Metrics: PRs merged: 1. Context switches/day this week: 2,3,2,4,2 -> avg 2.6. Mean debug time sample for two regressions last week: 3.5h (improved but not at 2h).
- Qualitative: deep work cadence is working; interruptions from ops pages still cause spikes.

Hypotheses & experiments tried
- Experiment A: 3x 90-min morning blocks, calendar status 'do not disturb' + Slack auto-response. Result: better concentration; PR review throughput doubled in block times.
- Experiment B: 'one small win' at EOD (15-30m) to tidy branches and write tests. Result: reduced friction next day. Keep.
- Hypothesis: explicit pre-review checklist reduces rework; testing by adding checklist to PR template (INF-PR-TEMP-1).

Retrospective notes (what worked / what didn't)
- Worked: Blocking deep work slots, explicit PR checklist, quick sync with SRE cleared infra choke.
- Didn't work: Trying to do too many async triages during deep blocks; Slack DND wasn't consistently enforced. Need a simple rule: if deep slot on calendar, only 1 allowed interruption (page/urgent).
- Learning: Short, measurable KRs help focus decisions: e.g., I deprioritized an unrelated refactor to protect KR progress.

Decisions made
- Prioritize KR1 over refactor X; schedule refactor X for next sprint window.
- Keep 3x 90-min deep blocks M/W/Th mornings for next cycle.
- Add a lightweight PR checklist and tag 'mini-okr' for related PRs to make tracking easier.

Open questions / follow-ups
- How to measure context switches more automatically? Could try a calendar->toggl sync or quick script to sample window focus events. (Action: prototype small Chrome extension or use RescueTime trial).
- Is 3-week horizon the right cadence? Maybe try a 2-week sprint experiment next time to tie to team cadence.
- Need to formalize the PR checklist in repo: who should own the PR template change? (Linked: PR #342 as a patch candidate.)

Action items (next 7 days)
- A1: Finish responses to Aria's review comments on PR#2 and push for merge by Thu (owner: me).
- A2: Add 'mini-okr' tag to PR template + add checklist item: "bench harness smoke + trace sampling" (owner: me + Devon for review).
- A3: Try RescueTime for 1 week to get an objective sample of context switches and focus time (owner: me).
- A4: Create short note for team retro: what blocking infra friction looked like and recommend short-term token rotation automation (owner: me).

Micro-retro prompt for sharing in 1:1 with manager
- 2 things that accelerated progress this cycle.
- 1 painpoint I want support on (infra automation / page noise).
- 1 experiment I want manager to try (help enforce deep-slot protection by nudging team on meeting scheduling).

Final quick metrics snapshot (as of 2025-03-05)
- KR1: 1/2 merged (50%).
- KR2: context switches/day avg across 3 weeks: ~3.5 -> trend downward (target <=3).
- KR3: mean debug time sample: 3.5h -> still above 2h target.

Quick sign-off: not perfect but moving. Keep the format short and repeatable. If this helps, I can convert to a 1-page TL;DR to share in the team weekly sync.

Raw daily micro-log (for traceability)
- 2025-02-11: D: start harness; C:5; T:1 block done (Tue)
- 2025-02-12: D: blocked by token; C:4; T:0
- 2025-02-13: D: debugging harness; C:6; T:1
- 2025-02-14: D: 2 deep slots, prototype run; C:3; T:2
- 2025-02-15: D: small triage + write smoke tests; C:7; T:0
- 2025-02-18: D: integrated runner; C:3; T:1
- 2025-02-19: D: PR -> Devon; C:2; T:1
- 2025-02-20: D: fix flake; C:4; T:0
- 2025-02-21: D: review sync w/ Aria; C:3; T:1
- 2025-02-22: D: rebase + e2e run; C:2; T:1
- 2025-02-25: D: PR#1 merged; C:2; T:2
- 2025-02-26: D: PR#2 address comments; C:3; T:1
- 2025-02-27: D: trace sampling work; C:2; T:1
- 2025-02-28: D: drafted retro note; C:4; T:0
- 2025-03-03: D: final review w/ Aria; C:2; T:2

Done for now. Short, noisy, and useful. Revisit next Monday and update KRs for next micro-cycle.

(Notes to self: capture this as a 1-paragraph template to make weekly sharing easier: 1 line progress, 1 line metric delta, 1 line blocker, 1 action.)
